A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LearNAT, with matching core methodology and benchmark results. Text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison. v1 ends after its references; v2 includes readable Appendices A–G, containing both relocated and new material.

before.justification: v1 reports original decomposition experiments, BIRD-dev and Spider-dev evaluations, component ablations, sensitivity analysis, and error analysis.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds protocol-specific comparisons, method variants, efficiency analyses, additional backbone evaluations, and repeated-run statistics.

M1.justification: The AST-guided synthesis and margin-DPO core remain, but v2 adds substantive extensions: execution-equivalent SQL rewriting in LearNAT+, semi-supervised self-training, and SQL-o1/Alpha-SQL inference integrations (Appendices F.1, F.5–F.6). v1's dedicated embedding-based Adaptive Demonstration Reasoning component is no longer specified; its relationship to v2's stated DAIL-SQL inference protocol is unexplained.

E1.justification: Both versions use BIRD-train for synthesis and BIRD-dev/Spider-dev for NL2SQL evaluation. Subtask-correctness evaluation also appears in both. The added experiments change supervision, SQL representations, backbones, or inference procedures within this coverage, without adding datasets, domains, or task requirements.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated comparisons with SynCoT, OmniSQL, SQL-o1, and Alpha-SQL, plus KTO/IPO and non-decomposition DPO controls. ZeroNL2SQL and MCS-SQL disappear from the headline comparison despite retained references. The subtask-verifier experiment changes from Qwen2-7B-Instruct to Sentence-Transformer and GLM-4.

E3.justification: v2 introduces protocol-specific comparisons, including inference-time MCTS, additional backbone configurations, a half-labeled BIRD training split, and multi-candidate self-consistency. It adds normalized inference-time, average-token, and EX-per-token metrics. The original benchmark splits, EX metric, and stated core training hyperparameters remain.

E4.justification: v2 adds controls testing decomposition versus ordinary DPO and MDPO versus KTO/IPO; analyses test SQL diversity, reduced supervision, backbone dependence, training-loss behavior, and inference accuracy–cost tradeoffs. The original error cases and AST-weight sensitivity analysis are retained through relocation. Demonstration-removal and random-demonstration ablations from v1 Table 5 are removed.

E5.justification: Unlike v1's point estimates without run-count information, v2 Appendix F.8/Table 12 systematically reports means and standard deviations over five experimental runs for all three principal model sizes across both benchmarks and difficulty groups. This newly documents uncertainty and run counts; it does not establish an increase over v1's actual number of runs.

E6.justification: Headline LearNAT scores and the 80.00% synthesis success rate are retained. Substantial new results include Alpha-SQL-protocol LearNAT scores of 68.4/90.6 on BIRD/Spider, LearNAT+ scores of 59.5/88.5, and semi-supervised scores of 54.8/83.4, alongside efficiency and variability results. These concern new settings. Removing MCS-SQL's 89.5 Spider score changes the headline ranking without changing LearNAT's scores.

T1.justification: v2 Equation 6 corrects the missing minus sign in v1 Equation 14's minimized SFT objective. The core AST definitions, similarity measures, and margin-DPO mathematics remain equivalent after relocation and notation changes. ADR's embedding/retrieval equations disappear with that section; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: v1 presents three components and broadly claims state-of-the-art advances. v2 foregrounds two components, explicitly targets resource-constrained model-level performance, and acknowledges that it does not achieve the best BIRD performance. It also strengthens novelty to the 'first framework' explicitly leveraging NL2SQL task decomposition. The 7B-model/GPT-4 comparability claim remains.

C2.justification: v2 develops interpretations concerning AST supervision's restriction of SQL diversity, semi-supervised applicability, backbone generality, and accuracy–token tradeoffs. It acknowledges higher token use than other model-level methods and a performance gap to CHASE-SQL. v1's limitations concerning unnecessary decomposition of simple queries and AST verification's inability to guarantee execution order are removed.

D1.justification: v2 provides a repository address and states that training/evaluation code and reproduction instructions are released, absent from v1. It newly identifies DAIL-SQL without-voting as the default inference protocol and documents MCTS integration details. Existing hardware and training hyperparameters are retained, while v1's initial manual-demonstration and retry details are omitted.

R1.justification: v2 substantially reframes positioning around model-level versus system-level solutions and process versus outcome rewards, adding discussion of SynCoT, OmniSQL, SQL-o1, Alpha-SQL, Reasoning-SQL, and Struct-LLM. It removes v1 Section 4.2's explicit acknowledgment of ODPO inspiration and the Amini et al. reference, changing attribution of the retained offset-loss design.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. v2 creates a dedicated motivation section, moves technical foundations and related work into appendices, relocates detailed experimental discussion, and adds ethics, reproducibility, and LLM-use statements. This substantially changes the narrative and document organization.

P2.justification: v2 switches from two-column to single-column presentation, substantially redraws the overview diagram, reorganizes benchmark columns and comparator groups, and adds colored performance differences. Numerous existing displays move to appendices. New comparison and analysis tables, a decomposition-strategy diagram, training curves, and a self-consistency accuracy–cost plot materially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: Protocol-specific comparisons, five-run variability reporting, diagnostic experiments, and code-access disclosure make v2 more assessable and reproducible. The net gain is limited by removal of the acknowledged ODPO antecedent and the strong MCS-SQL headline comparator, plus new reporting inconsistencies: Table 5's GLM-4 class counts and accuracies imply approximately 31.8% overall accuracy, not the reported 36.0%. These tradeoffs support a qualified improvement.
